chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The waiting period (iddah) of the one who has not yet menstruated, and the istihadah (one with irregular bleeding) who does not become pure, is three months. And the waiting period of the one who menstruates and whose menstruation becomes regular is three quru'. And the qur' is the collection of blood between the two menstruations.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: The one with istihadah (irregular uterine bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who has irregular menstruation or has not yet menstruated according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal distinction between 'qur'' (the interval between two menstruations) and 'tuhr' (purity), establishing a three-month waiting period for women with irregular or absent menstruation. It serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence regarding the calculation of iddah, emphasizing the practical application of menstrual cycles in determining marital status changes.
